title: Amadeus at National Theatre - Review
transcript: like nature national theatre designer zaboor a vacuum and face with the big space of the Olivia in Littleton auditoria they often feel the need to fill them with sets that dominate and slow down the plays but not so Amma dais here the stage is filled but with people and mainly an orchestra playing Mozart's sublime works Chloe Langford keeps the set simple and nothing distracts the two central roles of Salieri Mozart are acted brilliantly Lucy Maserati is the wily member of the establishment and you can feel his anguish at understanding the greatness of Mozart's music while being denied the talent to match it you can see why he wants to bring Mozart down and it's a difficult trick to pull off that Adam Gillan communicates the great composers annoying childlike innocence while still exceeding the power of his genius there's so much in Peter Schaffer's play that a revival is more than merited and it's brought out vividly in this bold production directed by Michael Longhurst I give it five stars you
